name: Renaissance
description: Revived classical philosophy and proportion, introducing linear perspective and naturalistic observation to European art.

name: Baroque
description: Used dramatic light and shadow, dynamic movement, and emotional intensity to evoke direct sensory response.

name: Ukiyo-e
description: Japanese woodblock prints and paintings depicting the fleeting world of urban life, landscapes, and theatre.

name: Impressionism
description: Captured fleeting sensations of natural light and everyday scenes through rapid, visible brushwork and unmixed color.

name: Post-Impressionism
description: Extended Impressionism's vivid palette while introducing structured geometry, symbolic depth, and subjective expression.

name: Fauvism
description: Liberated pure color from representational duty, prioritizing emotional vibrancy through raw, intense paintwork.

name: Cubism
description: Fractured objects into geometric facets to depict subjects from multiple viewpoints simultaneously.

name: Surrealism
description: Bridged conscious reality and the unconscious mind through dreamlike juxtapositions and automatism.

name: Abstract Expressionism
description: Conveyed universal psychological themes through gestural mark-making, spontaneous action, and expansive color fields.

name: Pop Art
description: Blurred the boundary between high art and consumer culture by repurposing mass media, comics, and commercial goods.

name: Minimalism
description: Stripped artwork to its purest geometric forms and industrial materials, removing metaphor and artist gesture.

name: Bauhaus
description: Bridged fine arts, craft, and industrial technology under the ideal of unified, functional design.

name: Art Nouveau
description: Drew inspiration from organic structures, featuring curvilinear whiplash rhythms and stylized floral motifs.

name: Mono-ha
description: Japanese contemporary movement exploring relations between unaltered natural and industrial materials in physical space.
